entry.title: How to repair your items and vehicles in Dune Awakening
entry.summary:
Dune Awakening, staying true to the MMO genre, offers plenty of items and vehicles to unlock, but it's important to repair all of them throughout your journey.
All items, including your vehicle, will take damage over time. Their durability will go down, and they can stop functioning without repairs. The process of repairs varies slightly depending on whether it's an item or your vehicle. You can also repair building parts, but that's done with the crafting tool. Let's first look at how to repair general items, followed by vehicles.
Table of contents How to repair items in Dune Awakening How to repair your vehicles in Dune Awakening
How to repair items in Dune Awakening
For repairs, you'll need a Repair Station. The blueprint has to be researched first from the Research section. To do so, complete the Maintenance quest in the Vermillius Gap Journey. Once done, you'll get the option to research and craft the Repair Station.
Place the Repair Station in your base and interact with it. Place the item you want to repair and supply the required raw materials. The process will take a little while to complete, and your items will be as good as new. The amount of resources you need will vary based on the item and its condition.
Screenshot via Funcom
How to repair your vehicles in Dune Awakening
Whether you're using an Ornithopter or a bike, vehicles will take damage. You'll have to repair them before major journeys to prevent them from breaking down. For vehicles, you don't need a Repair Station. Instead, your Welding Tool should be more than good enough. For most vehicles, you'll need Welding Wire.
The Fabricator produces both the Welding Tool and Welding Wire. The Fabricator unlocks pretty quickly (again, research it to unlock the blueprint), and you can position it on your base. Always craft plenty of Welding Wires on your travels, as repairing vehicles can quickly empty your stock.

entry.title: How to get the Holtzman Amplifier in Dune Awakening
entry.summary:
The Holtzman Amplifier is an important quest item in Dune Awakening if you want to complete the Scrap Mettle series of quests.
It's easy to miss, as completing this set of missions is not part of the main storyline. Instead, these side contracts will help you earn extra rewards to boost your early game progression. Let's learn how to find and use the Holtzman Amplifier on your journey in Arrakis. We begin by starting the Scrap Mettle: Wrecking Crew quest.
Dune Awakening Scrap Mettle: Wrecking Crew quest guide
Starting the Scrap Mettle: Wrecking Crew quest is pretty simple: travel to Griffin's Reach and complete the first part of the Scrap Mettle: Copper Required (self-explanatory). This will begin the Wrecking Crew quest. Next up, you'll make your way to Wreck of the Alcyon in Dune Awakening.
Screenshot via Funcom
The exact location is shown in the screenshot above. Travel to the east of the Griffin's Reach at Hagga Basin South. It's quite a journey, so carry a lot of water. Going north through the rocky structures is the quickest way, but avoid the Sandworms (constantly moving and keeping track of the radar).
The Wreck of the Alcyon has a few Scavengers; finish them first. Then, loot all the available stuff and look for the Holtzman Amplifier. There's a chance for the enemies to respawn if you take too long, so keep that in mind.
Go to the main entrance of the location, and then go right towards the back of the ship. You'll find a room with the yellow globe hologram in it. Continue to the back wall, and you'll see a small chest. Open the chest, and you'll get the Holtzman Amplifier. Make sure to loot the other chests, as you'll find plenty of valuable items that can be used for crafting blueprints.
Using it isn't rocket science; just return to Griffin's Reach and deliver it, which automatically begins the Scrap Mettle: Fremen Fields quest.

entry.title: What was your biggest Summer Games Fest reveal?
entry.summary:
Summer Games Fest has now concluded, and we have had a bunch of new game reveals across the multiple shows, from the big Summer Games Fest main show, all the way to the PlayStation State of Play, Xbox Showcase, Wholesome Direct, and more.
There have been multiple game reveals at the event, some good, some bad, and many that might become forgettable as time passes. But as the dust begins to settle on the event, I think it's important to discuss what was our most memorable, or biggest, game reveal from every show over the past few days, for good or bad reasons.
For me, there were a few games that stuck out at the time, either because the reveal surprised me, or because it was a game I had genuine interest in. Most of the Xbox Games Showcase was a treat, with trailer after trailer showcasing titles like Persona 4 Revival, Grounded 2, Super Meat Boy 3D, and a host of other games that excited my friends and me as we watched. It was arguably the best presentation of the entire weekend by far.
There were also indie darlings like Big Walk that got a proper gameplayer trailer in some of the smaller shows, and I imagine a lot of people will be talking about the Resident Evil 9 reveal at the end of the Summer Games Fest main showcase, even if most of the show felt lacklustre at times.
Theres also been a slew of controversal reveals for one reason or another, such as Game Freak's Xbox game reveal of Beast of Reincarnation, which as you can imagine has pissed off a lot of Pokémon fans for the graphics comparisons between it and the Pokémon series as a whole.
A lot of fans were also surprised to see a lack of Switch 2 and Switch 2 game reveals as a whole, but... come on. The console has only been out for a matter of days at this point. You expect brand new announcements so soon? Wait till Gamescom.
But enough talking, what was your biggest pick from the various shows? Let us know in the comments below.

entry.title: Xbox’s Showcase was far better than Summer Games Fest in every single way, don’t you agree?
entry.summary:
The first week and a bit of June is full of game showcases and announcements to get fans hyped. Summer Games Fest had some fantastic highlights, with Resident Evil 9: Requiem and Lies of P: Overture shadow-dropping being two of several focal points. The June 8 Xbox Showcase, though, is on an entirely different level.
Despite Summer Games Fest having some of the most hyped-up announcements anyone could've expected, it was a slow burn to get to those points. There were plenty of trailers, but with the event spanning several hours, it took a while to get to them. Compare this to the Xbox Showcase's back-to-back trailers for massive titles like Persona 4 Revival, a new Call of Duty, and Grounded 2. It generated more hype in its first hour than SGF did in its entire runtime.
Image via Xbox
Don't get me wrong—I have highlights from both showcases. Seeing Sonic Racing CrossWorlds feature both Hatsune Miku and Minecraft within it during SGF was a hilarious, unexpected twist that had me chuckling for a while. My favorite part of the Xbox Games Showcase, on the other hand, was the announcement of Grounded 2, especially after remembering how much I enjoyed playing the first game with friends. One of those friends was also very excited about Planet of Lana 2, reminding me that I need to play it at some point.
Showcases and festivals make video gaming much more fun. While sure, I found the Xbox Showcase more interesting overall, I still had an absolute blast with SGF. My interest in these almost came close to my overwhelming joy for the Wholesome Direct this past Saturday, but that's an entirely separate conversation.

entry.title: Could The Witcher 4's Kelpie be the best video game horse yet? We asked an expert
entry.summary:
If you caught The Witcher 4's tech demo at yesterday's Unreal showcase, you likely spent an above-average amount of time for a Tuesday being impressed by horse muscles. Still, however excited you were about that horse, I'd wager you weren't quite as happy as Alice Ruppert - consultant on the upcoming Windstorm: The Legend of Khiimori, and owner of the very best website about video game horses on the internet. Ruppert's initial reaction? "Tears of joy in my eyes when they showed the slow mo horse movement". "I'm a big fan of the of the Witcher books, and so I knew that Ciri has a horse named Kelpie in the books," Ruppert tells me over a call, "so, that's part of it". But it's also the care that's been put in. "Like: here's our gorgeous horse. We care about it, and we know you care about it. And that made me feel very seen. I think that's what brought the tears to my eyes. Of course, I am so profoundly a horse girl that you can, depending on my mood of the day, you can show me a slow mo footage of a horse galloping and I will cry in any case. That's just my horse appreciation brain rot."

entry.title: ScummVM 2.9.1 “Slappin da BASS” is here!
entry.summary: Get ready to jam and slap da BASS! Yes, it is this time of the year again! Please welcome the first ScummVM release of the year: ScummVM 2.9.1. This maintenance release mainly focused on fixing bugs that our developers and users have uncovered since our last stable release. As usual, several engines and platforms received their fair share of bug fixes and improvements: AGI, AGS, Asylum, BAGEL, Bladerunner, Hopkins, MADS, NGI, SCI, SCUMM, Sky, Sword1, Tetraedge, Tinsel, Tucker, TwinE, and TWP. Our porters also went on a bug-hunting spree, so all we can provide is a small summary of the latest and greatest fixes! The Nintendo 3DS (yes, we do not care about end-of-life dates!) has the GUI appropriately displayed if it is configured to use the top screen only. Android now provides an option to save and restore your configuration file and save games, and the vast majority of older Android devices will see increased performance thanks to the ARM NEON optimizations, which are now enabled by default. And the Beneath a Steel Sky game is not crashing in the intro anymore! The Atari port received some internal backend, GUI, and audio fixes. Speaking of audio: iOS/iPad will now always properly recognize FluidSynth soundfonts, macOS has support for Audio CD playback from original discs on Snow Leopard and earlier, and Windows 9x (yes, EOL…) can use FLAC files again! The detailed list of improvements is available here. Head over to our downloads page and grab it while it’s hot! As usual, macOS and Windows users can update ScummVM with our integrated, magical auto-upgrade solution. >

entry.title: A new game for testing. Believe It Or Not
entry.summary: Robert Ripley, a famous traveler and collector of rarities. One day, during a trip in Egypt, Ripley is attacked by mysterious Chinese assassins. The trail will lead him and his Chinese girlfriend Mei Chen on a chase around the world, in a race against time to prevent the greatest theft of all time, the First Emperor's seal, which could plunge the world into chaos. The ScummVM Team is pleased to announce full support for Ripley's Believe It Or Not! The Secret of Master Lu, the other classic game, besides Orion Burger, by Sanctuary Woods. As with Orion Burger, it adds a few niceties that the original didn't have, such as mouse wheel handling, and using the spacebar to skip walk animations. Help us test the game by grabbing a daily build. Read through our testing guidelines. The game's logic was all hardcoded, and proved even more complicated than that of Orion Burger, so we really need people to try all sorts of weird actions, and make sure the game handles everything correctly and matches the original implementation. And please take some screenshots along the way. Good luck. If you fail to prevent the seal falling into evil hands, it could be used to unite all Asia under a single ruler, thirsty for conquest. >

entry.title: Two more Nancy Drew Mysteries solved!
entry.summary: Are you ready for more sleuthing with everyone’s favorite teenage detective? We’re excited to announce that Nancy Drew: Secret of the Scarlet Hand and Nancy Drew: Ghost Dogs of Moon Lake are now ready for public testing! Furthermore, it's now possible to enable the ScummVM save/load screens instead of the original ones, to take advantage of additional features when saving or loading. In Nancy Drew: Secret of the Scarlet Hand, Nancy takes on the role of an intern at a Washington D.C. museum, where a mysterious theft sets off a series of clues leading deep into the secrets of ancient Maya artifacts. In Nancy Drew: Ghost Dogs of Moon Lake, Nancy finds herself investigating a haunted cabin surrounded by eerie howls and ghostly canine apparitions. The games are available for purchase through HeR Interactive’s website or Steam. Or if you already own a CD copy of the games, their English and Russian variants will also work. To play them with ScummVM, you will need a daily development build. As always, if you encounter any issues, please submit a bug report to our issue tracker. >
